# PostHog — Style Reference

> An oat-paper window floating over painted wallpaper, with an amber key pressed into it. A rounded grotesk set at weight 500 to 800 sits on an #eeefe9 oat canvas, with 1px olive-gray hairlines and a single amber keycap that physically depresses.

**Theme:** light

Values are measured from the live site and normalized; names, roles and recommendations are interpretation. Font lists are independent, not paired by position. Example prompts describe reconstructions, not the site's source code.

PostHog speaks a desktop-operating-system product language. The home page is a window, not a page. It floats over a painted green wallpaper and is flanked by desktop icons, with a menubar pinned along the top edge. The stack runs from an #eeefe9 oat canvas to #fdfdf8 paper cards and #ffffff panels, and #e5e7e0 stone strips head each panel. The chromatic budget is one warm hue family in four steps: amber face #eb9d2a, ochre depth #cd8407, bronze edge #b17816 and ember signal #f54e00. That family is rationed to the primary action, the active tab and highlighter marks. Categorical product hues stay inside mockups. RoundHog carries everything at weight 500 for reading and 700 to 800 for headings, with −0.025em tracking above 18px. The scale steps roughly a Major Third, from 18px to 36px in three moves. Shape is near-sharp, mostly 4px radii. Elevation uses real shadows deployed like a window manager, plus one hard-edged keycap ledge. The result reads as software you are using rather than a marketing page you are scrolling.

## Tokens — Colors

| Name | Value | Token | Role |
|---|---|---|---|
| Fog Canvas | `#eeefe9` | `--color-fog-canvas` | Body background and the main window surface behind every section — a warm olive-tinted off-white that keeps the whole system from reading as clinical white. |
| Paper Card | `#fdfdf8` | `--color-paper-card` | Logo panels, issue cards, live-event tables and mockup bodies, with 43 background uses — the most-used surface, one quiet step brighter than the canvas. |
| Quartz White | `#ffffff` | `--color-quartz-white` | Setup panel, secondary keycap face, desktop-icon labels on wallpaper, with 26 background uses — reserved for the brightest elevated layer. Do not use it as page canvas. |
| Stone Strip | `#e5e7e0` | `--color-stone-strip` | Panel header strips ("Colorful logos", "Live events"), table heads and inactive tab wells — tonal separation that replaces a heavier divider line. |
| Ink | `#111111` | `--color-ink` | Body copy inside cards, h3 titles and hero CTA labels, with 114 uses — near-black rather than pure #000000, which matches the warm canvas. |
| Graphite Nav | `#23251d` | `--color-graphite-nav` | Menubar items, header CTA label and logo fill — an olive-black that ties chrome to the green-gray neutrals rather than to cool gray. |
| Pewter Caption | `#65675e` | `--color-pewter-caption` | Secondary paragraphs, social-proof subline and card metadata, with 143 uses — the workhorse text color, out-counting Ink. |
| Ash Hint | `#9ea096` | `--color-ash-hint` | Monospace timestamps, column labels and icon tint, with 84 uses — tertiary text that recedes without disappearing. Do not use it for body copy below 14px. |
| Pebble Border | `#bfc1b7` | `--color-pebble-border` | Card outlines, code chips, table rules and window edges, with 72 uses at 1px — the system's only line color, olive-gray rather than neutral gray. |
| Sunbeam Amber | `#eb9d2a` | `--color-sunbeam-amber` | Primary keycap face, the swap icon ring and highlighter tints, with 17 background uses — the brand accent. Keep it on actions and marks, never on large surfaces. |
| Ochre Key | `#cd8407` | `--color-ochre-key` | The ledge under the amber keycap face and link color — a darker step that renders depth when the face lifts. Do not use it as a standalone button fill. |
| Bronze Edge | `#b17816` | `--color-bronze-edge` | 1px border on primary and secondary keycaps, with 16 uses — the outline that makes white and amber buttons read as the same physical object. |
| Ember Signal | `#f54e00` | `--color-ember-signal` | Active showcase tab, the thick frame around the active panel and the "build better products" highlight — the loudest hue on the page, rationed to one active state per view. |

Two heading and lead colors, #111827 on h1 and h2 and #374151 on the hero paragraph, are Tailwind gray inheritances and not system tokens. Build headings in Ink and leads in Pewter Caption. Four mockup-only hues are decorative and not system tokens: #2f80fa blue, #6aa84f green, #b62ad9 purple and #f35454 red.

## Tokens — Typography

### RoundHog — the single proprietary voice for display, UI and body · `--font-roundhog`

- **Substitute:** Figtree at 500 for body and 800 for display, Nunito Sans at 600 for body and 800 for display, or Inter at 500 for body and 800 for display. RoundHog draws true to nominal weight, with softened terminals that make 500 read warmer than Inter's 500. Choose Figtree first, because its open apertures match. Do not drop body copy to 400, which reads visibly thinner than the original.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700, 800
- **Sizes:** 10.5px, 11px, 12px, 13px, 14px, 15px, 16px, 17px, 18px, 22px, 24px, 30px, 36px
- **Line height:** 1.0 to 1.78. Body runs 1.43 to 1.5 and display 1.11.
- **Letter spacing:** −0.9px at 36px, −0.75px at 30px, −0.6px at 24px, −0.45px at 18px (h3 variant), normal at 17px and below
- **Role:** Weight 500 as the reading default is the anti-convention move. Most SaaS sets body at 400, and the extra stroke here gives paragraphs a sturdy, slightly chunky voice that matches the cartoon hedgehog brand. Headings jump to 700 and 800 instead of the 600 most product sites stop at. The top of the scale therefore hits hard and the measure stays short, 504px in the hero. Tracking is a constant −0.025em above 18px, the Tailwind tracking-tight convention, applied mechanically rather than optically. The step sizes of 18, 24, 30 and 36px run roughly 1.33, 1.25 and 1.2, a compressed Major Third that tops out at only 36px. That is small for a hero by convention, and deliberately so: windows do not shout.

### ui-monospace — system mono for metadata, labels and terminal text · `--font-ui-mono`

- **Substitute:** JetBrains Mono at 500, IBM Plex Mono at 500 or Geist Mono at 500. The native stack (SF Mono or Menlo) renders medium-light, so stay at 500 and avoid 400.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 700
- **Sizes:** 9px, 11px, 12px, 15px
- **Line height:** 1.0, 1.33, 1.5, 1.78
- **Letter spacing:** normal at all sizes
- **Role:** With 143 uses at weight 500, the system mono is the second voice of the site. It carries timestamps, "acme/web" repo labels, table column heads and install commands. Using the OS mono instead of a webfont is consistent with the desktop thesis, because the metadata literally looks like the user's terminal. The 11px size with a loose 1.78 leading is the signature, giving tiny text room to breathe inside dense mockups.

### Source Code Pro — webfont mono for code chips inside product mockups · `--font-source-code-pro`

- **Substitute:** Source Code Pro itself (open source) at 500, or Fira Code at 500.
- **Weights:** 400, 500, 600, 700
- **Sizes:** 11.5px, 14px
- **Line height:** 1.43 at 14px, 2.43 at 11.5px
- **Letter spacing:** normal at all sizes
- **Role:** Source Code Pro is confined to commit-scope chips such as `fix(auth)` and `feat(billing)`, plus inline code. The 11.5px value is a 14px chip rendered inside a mockup scaled to about 0.82. The fractional sizes across the extracted data (11.52px, 12.07px, 13.17px) are all transform artifacts of that scaling, not tokens. Pairing a second mono beside the system mono separates "content the product shows" from "chrome the OS shows".

### Type Scale

| Role | Family | Weight | Size | Line Height | Letter Spacing | Token |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| small | ui-monospace | 500 | 11px | 1.78 | 0px | `--text-small` |
| caption | RoundHog | 500 | 12px | 1.33 | 0px | `--text-caption` |
| body-sm | RoundHog | 500 | 13px | 1.25 | 0px | `--text-body-sm` |
| body | RoundHog | 500 | 14px | 1.43 | 0px | `--text-body` |
| body-lg | RoundHog | 500 | 17px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-body-lg` |
| subheading | RoundHog | 500 | 18px | 1.5 | 0px | `--text-subheading` |
| heading-sm | RoundHog | 700 | 18px | 1.56 | 0px | `--text-heading-sm` |
| heading | RoundHog | 700 | 24px | 1.33 | -0.6px | `--text-heading` |
| heading-lg | RoundHog | 700 | 30px | 1.33 | -0.75px | `--text-heading-lg` |
| display | RoundHog | 800 | 36px | 1.11 | -0.9px | `--text-display` |

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Frame every page as a window: 1200px wide, #eeefe9 fill, 6px radius, `--shadow-xl` drop over imagery — the desktop metaphor is the brand, not a hero gimmick.
- Build every primary action as a keycap: #eb9d2a face over a #cd8407 ledge, 1px #b17816 border, 8px radius — the 2px lift that collapses on press is non-negotiable.
- Set reading text in RoundHog at weight 500, 14px in cards and 17px in leads — the heavier default stroke gives copy the sturdy, friendly voice that 400 loses.
- Separate surfaces with 1px #bfc1b7 hairlines and a #e5e7e0 header strip — tonal steps of 4% do the layering that most systems hand to shadows.
- Keep radii at 4px for cards, badges and chips, and 6px for windows and buttons — the near-sharp vocabulary reads as desktop software rather than a consumer app.
- Use ui-monospace 11px at weight 500 in #9ea096 for timestamps, repo paths and column labels — metadata should look like it came from a terminal.
- Emphasize headline phrases with 10% tint highlighter blocks at a 2px radius — annotation replaces gradient text and weight jumps.

### Don't

- Don't lay the page directly on full-bleed white sections — dropping the wallpaper-plus-window frame turns an operating system into a generic landing page and erases the thesis.
- Don't flatten the keycap into a plain #eb9d2a rectangle with no #cd8407 ledge — the button stops feeling pressable and collides with the amber highlighter marks.
- Don't round cards to 12px or 16px "to soften" them — the 4px rule is what makes the 9999px icon buttons and the 20px third-party mockup windows read as intentional outliers.
- Don't use #f54e00 Ember for more than one active element per view — once a second tab or button turns ember, state signalling collapses into decoration.
- Don't swap the olive-gray neutrals (#65675e, #bfc1b7) for cool Tailwind grays — the warm-green cast tying chrome to the wallpaper disappears instantly.
- Don't push the display headline past 36px or below weight 800 — the window holds a compact, assertive title, and a 72px hero would never fit the desktop scale.
- Don't let the decorative mockup hues (#2f80fa, #b62ad9, #6aa84f) leak into buttons or links — they belong to product icons inside screenshots, and promoting them dilutes the single warm family.

## Agent Prompt Guide

**Quick Color Reference**
- canvas: #eeefe9 (Fog Canvas)
- card surface: #fdfdf8 (Paper Card)
- primary text: #111111 (Ink)
- secondary text: #65675e (Pewter Caption)
- border: #bfc1b7 (Pebble Border)
- active state: #f54e00 (Ember Signal)
- primary action: #eb9d2a (filled action)

**Color in Data**
Charts take categorical hues only as 10% tint fills with a 1px solid stroke of the same hue. Axes, labels and gridlines stay in #9ea096 and #bfc1b7, and amber and ember are kept out of data so the keycap remains the loudest object on any page.

**Example Component Prompts**

1. Build a Primary Action Button as a keycap. Create an outer `<a>` 47px tall with background #cd8407, a 1px solid #b17816 border and an 8px border-radius. Inside it, place a `<span>` filling the button with background #eb9d2a, a 1px solid #b17816 border, an 8px radius and transform translateY(-2px). Set the label "Get started" centred in RoundHog (fallback Figtree) at 18px, weight 500, line-height 1.5 and color #111111, with 16px horizontal padding. On hover, translateY(-4px). On active, translateY(0). Add no blur shadow.

2. Build a hero inside an application window. Make the outer window 1200px wide with background #eeefe9, a 1px solid #bfc1b7 border, a 6px radius and box-shadow 0px 25px 50px -12px rgba(0,0,0,0.25), centred over a full-bleed painted green background image. Use a 1024px inner column with 64px top padding. The left column, 504px wide, holds an h1 "Your product's context layer" in RoundHog 36px, weight 800, line-height 1.11, letter-spacing -0.9px, color #111111. Wrap "context layer" in a highlight with background #2f80fa1a and a 2px radius. Follow it with a 17px weight-500 lead in #65675e at line-height 1.5, a 24px gap, then an 18px weight-500 line in #65675e. The right column holds a 448px-wide card with background #ffffff, a 1px #bfc1b7 border, a 4px radius, 16px padding and box-shadow 0px 20px 25px -5px rgba(0,0,0,0.1), 0px 8px 10px -6px rgba(0,0,0,0.1). Give it an 18px weight-700 title, three 14px weight-500 checklist rows with an 8px gap, then the amber keycap and a white keycap (#ffffff face, 1px #b17816 border, 8px radius) side by side with an 8px gap.

3. Build an issue card list. Use a container with background #e5e7e0, a 1px #bfc1b7 border, a 4px radius and 12px padding. Each card has background #fdfdf8, a 1px #bfc1b7 border, a 4px radius, 16px padding and an 8px gap between cards. Row one holds a 25px-square priority badge (4px radius, 1px border rgba of the hue at 40%, 10% tint fill, RoundHog 12px weight 600, P3 in #f54e00 on #eb9d2a1a), then a code chip (transparent, 1px #bfc1b7 border, 4px radius, padding 0 4px, Source Code Pro 14px weight 500, #111111), then a title in RoundHog 14px weight 600 #111111. Row two is a 13px weight-500 description in #65675e. Row three shows "acme/web" in ui-monospace 11px weight 500 #9ea096 on the left and "Just now" right-aligned in the same style.

4. Build the OS menubar. Make a full-width bar 40px tall with background #eeefe9 and a 1px bottom border in #bfc1b7, with 12px horizontal padding. On the left, place the logo glyph in #23251d at 24px, then menu buttons for Products, Pricing, Docs, Community, Company and More. Each button is transparent, 28px tall, padding 2px 8px, 4px radius, RoundHog 13px weight 500, color #23251d, with a #e5e7e0 background on hover. On the right, place a compact keycap "Get started – free" (32px tall, 6px radius, #eb9d2a face over #cd8407, 1px #b17816 border, 16px weight-500 label in #23251d), then three 26px circular icon buttons with a 9999px radius and 4px padding, all separated by an 8px gap.

| md | `0px 4px 6px -1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), 0px 2px 4px -2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)` | `--shadow-md` |
| lg | `0px 20px 25px -5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), 0px 8px 10px -6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)` | `--shadow-lg` |
| xl | `0px 25px 50px -12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25)` | `--shadow-xl` |

### Layout

- **Page max-width:** 1200px (672–1200px)
- **Section gap:** 64px (48–96px)
- **Card padding:** 16px (12–24px)
- **Element gap:** 8px (4–12px)

## Components

### Keycap Button — Amber (Primary)

**Role:** The one action per view.

A physical, pressable key. The base layer is #cd8407 Ochre Key with a 1px #b17816 Bronze Edge border and an 8px radius, measured at 47px tall. A #eb9d2a Sunbeam Amber face sits on top, lifted 2px to expose an ochre ledge underneath. The label is RoundHog 18px at weight 500 in #111111 Ink, centred with 16px horizontal padding, and there is no blur shadow. The compact menubar variant is 32px tall with a 6px radius and a 16px label. The construction communicates tactility over flatness: it is the only element on the page that moves in z when clicked.

### Keycap Button — White (Secondary)

**Role:** Alternative path beside primary.

The same key, different cap. It takes a #ffffff Quartz White face with the identical 1px #b17816 Bronze Edge border, the same 8px radius and 47px height, and a RoundHog 18px label at weight 500 in #111111. The face sits over the 2.5px ledge in rgba(210, 211, 204, 1) defined as `--shadow-sm`. A 32px small variant labelled "Open Customers" uses a 13px label and the 6px radius. Sharing the bronze border with the primary is deliberate, because both buttons read as keys from one keyboard and differ only in cap color.

### OS Menubar — Navigation Bar

**Role:** Global chrome pinned across top.

A desktop menubar, not a website header. It spans the full 1920px viewport on a translucent Fog Canvas strip about 40px tall (estimated). The PostHog glyph sits left, followed by text buttons for Products, Pricing, Docs, Community, Company and More. Each button is transparent with #23251d Graphite Nav text in RoundHog 13px at weight 500, padding 2px 8px, a 4px radius and 28px height. The compact amber keycap sits right, beside 26px circular icon buttons for search, chat and account at a 9999px radius. It behaves like operating-system chrome, with menus that open rather than pages that load.

### Desktop Icon Launcher

**Role:** Secondary navigation as desktop shortcuts.

Icons on wallpaper. Two vertical columns sit outside the window on the painted backdrop. The left column holds Home, MCP, Self-driving, Pricing, Docs, Demo and Talk to a human. The right column holds About us, Changelog, Company handbook, Store, Careers and Trash. Each entry is a 32px monochrome line-art glyph above a #ffffff label in RoundHog 16px at weight 500, with no background, no border and a 60px hit height. Placing navigation as desktop shortcuts is the thesis made literal, and the Trash icon is the wink that confirms it.

### Application Window — Page Container

**Role:** The home page as a window.

The signature surface. A 1200px-wide panel of #eeefe9 Fog Canvas carries a 6px sections radius, a 1px #bfc1b7 Pebble Border and the `--shadow-xl` drop of 0px 25px 50px −12px at 25% black. Small maximize and close controls sit top-right in #9ea096 Ash Hint. Inside, a 1024px content column holds 64px section gaps and a 672px text measure. Treat every new top-level page as another window, scrollable internally and floating over wallpaper.

### Paper Card — Main Content Card

**Role:** Holds lists, logos, tables, mockups.

Paper on oat. The card uses #fdfdf8 Paper Card fill, a 1px #bfc1b7 border and a 4px radius, with no shadow beyond the optional 1px `--shadow-subtle`. Padding is 16px. Split variants add a #e5e7e0 Stone Strip header bar in RoundHog 13px at weight 600, with a 1px vertical Pebble divider between columns. The near-zero contrast step between #eeefe9 and #fdfdf8 is intentional, because the hairline does the separating and the fill only warms it.

### Setup Panel — Floating Card

**Role:** Conversion panel beside hero copy.

The brightest object on the page. A #ffffff Quartz White panel carries a 4px radius, a 1px #bfc1b7 border, the `--shadow-lg` drop and 16px padding. A RoundHog 18px title at weight 700 in Ink sits above a checklist of 14px weight-500 rows with olive check glyphs. Below it, the amber and white keycaps sit side by side with an 8px gap. Elevating this one card above the window plane, while the rest of the content sits flat, tells the eye exactly where the decision lives.

### Tabbed Showcase Frame — Ember (System Outlier)

**Role:** Active product demo panel.

The loud exception. Inactive tabs are plain #65675e text in RoundHog 14px at weight 600. The active tab fills #f54e00 Ember Signal with #ffffff text and a 6px top-only radius (6px 6px 0 0). It connects into a 6px-thick ember frame around a #fdfdf8 demo panel. This is the only place a saturated fill exceeds button scale. It is allowed because it marks state, not decoration: one tab is live, and the frame moves when the tab changes.

### Highlighter Mark

**Role:** Inline emphasis in headlines.

Marker on paper. Key phrases such as "context layer", "analytics, errors, replays" and "build better products" sit on a translucent rectangle with a 2px smallElements radius. The rectangle takes 10% tint fills of the phrase's hue: amber tint #eb9d2a1a, blue tint #2f80fa1a, and ember text on amber tint. These are derived tints and not separate tokens. Text weight is unchanged at 800 or 500. Emphasis comes from the stroke of a highlighter rather than from bolding or gradient text, consistent with the hand-annotated tone.

### Priority Badge

**Role:** Severity tag on issue cards.

A tiny tinted square. It measures 25px on each side with a 4px radius and a 1px border at 40% of the hue over a 10% tint fill. The label is RoundHog 12px at weight 600. P3 uses #f54e00 Ember text on an amber tint, and P2 uses the decorative red #f35454 on its tint. Badges stay square instead of pill-shaped, following the system's 4px rule rather than the pill convention most dashboards use.

### Code Chip

**Role:** Commit scope and inline code.

Mono in a box. The chip is transparent with a 1px #bfc1b7 border, a 4px radius and 0 4px padding at native scale. It uses Source Code Pro 14px at weight 500 in #111111, rendered at 11.5px inside scaled mockups. It reads as git output pasted into the UI, which tells developers the demo is real tooling rather than an illustration.

### Live Events Table

**Role:** Streaming data inside mockup.

A terminal log as a table. It sits on a #fdfdf8 body with a #e5e7e0 Stone Strip header row holding uppercase 11px ui-monospace column labels in #9ea096. Rows are 1px #bfc1b7-ruled at about 30px height. Each row has a 16px source icon on a colored rounded tile, an event name in RoundHog 13px at weight 600, and mono 11px values in #65675e. Older rows fade toward #9ea096. Density here is deliberately higher than the marketing copy around it, proving the product handles volume.

## Do's and Don'ts

### Do

- Frame every page as a window: 1200px wide, #eeefe9 fill, 6px radius, `--shadow-xl` drop over imagery — the desktop metaphor is the brand, not a hero gimmick.
- Build every primary action as a keycap: #eb9d2a face over a #cd8407 ledge, 1px #b17816 border, 8px radius — the 2px lift that collapses on press is non-negotiable.
- Set reading text in RoundHog at weight 500, 14px in cards and 17px in leads — the heavier default stroke gives copy the sturdy, friendly voice that 400 loses.
- Separate surfaces with 1px #bfc1b7 hairlines and a #e5e7e0 header strip — tonal steps of 4% do the layering that most systems hand to shadows.
- Keep radii at 4px for cards, badges and chips, and 6px for windows and buttons — the near-sharp vocabulary reads as desktop software rather than a consumer app.
- Use ui-monospace 11px at weight 500 in #9ea096 for timestamps, repo paths and column labels — metadata should look like it came from a terminal.
- Emphasize headline phrases with 10% tint highlighter blocks at a 2px radius — annotation replaces gradient text and weight jumps.

### Don't

- Don't lay the page directly on full-bleed white sections — dropping the wallpaper-plus-window frame turns an operating system into a generic landing page and erases the thesis.
- Don't flatten the keycap into a plain #eb9d2a rectangle with no #cd8407 ledge — the button stops feeling pressable and collides with the amber highlighter marks.
- Don't round cards to 12px or 16px "to soften" them — the 4px rule is what makes the 9999px icon buttons and the 20px third-party mockup windows read as intentional outliers.
- Don't use #f54e00 Ember for more than one active element per view — once a second tab or button turns ember, state signalling collapses into decoration.
- Don't swap the olive-gray neutrals (#65675e, #bfc1b7) for cool Tailwind grays — the warm-green cast tying chrome to the wallpaper disappears instantly.
- Don't push the display headline past 36px or below weight 800 — the window holds a compact, assertive title, and a 72px hero would never fit the desktop scale.
- Don't let the decorative mockup hues (#2f80fa, #b62ad9, #6aa84f) leak into buttons or links — they belong to product icons inside screenshots, and promoting them dilutes the single warm family.

## Elevation

- **Application window over wallpaper:** `0px 25px 50px -12px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25)`
- **Floating setup panel and popovers:** `0px 20px 25px -5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), 0px 8px 10px -6px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)`
- **Menus and small floating tooltips:** `0px 4px 6px -1px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1), 0px 2px 4px -2px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.1)`
- **Keycap ledge on secondary buttons:** `0px 2.5px 0px 0px rgba(210, 211, 204, 1)`
- **Dock app icons in mockups:** `inset 0px 0px 0px 0.5px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25), 0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.25)`
- **Resting cards and tables:** `0px 1px 2px 0px rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.05)`

The rule: blur shadows mark windows and floating panels in proportion to their z-height, as a window manager would. Hard zero-blur shadows mark only pressable keys.

## Imagery

The home page uses almost no photography. The single exception is the painted, brush-textured green-teal wallpaper behind the window, which is decorative and not a system token. Everything inside the window is a live-looking product mockup built in HTML, never a flat screenshot. These include issue lists, a dark mobile chat app, a live-events table, box-plot charts and a Claude-style chat window with a macOS dock. Native mockups sit on #fdfdf8 with 1px #bfc1b7 borders and 4px radii. Third-party app imitations take a 20px radius and traffic-light controls to signal "someone else's software". Icons are monochrome 1.5px line glyphs, with product-category icons given single decorative hues. There are no gradient orbs or glows. The narrative is that PostHog runs inside your computer and plugs into the tools you already have open.

## Layout

The window caps at 1200px and centres over full-bleed wallpaper. Inside it sits a 1024px content column with a 672px text measure, and sections stack at a 64px gap. The hero splits two columns: the 36px display headline, a 17px lead and the social line sit left on a 504px measure, and the floating #ffffff setup panel sits right. Sections do not alternate backgrounds. They alternate between text-led blocks and wide mockup panels on one continuous #eeefe9 plane. Logo rows use a two-panel split of three-up then two-up wordmarks, while the tool strip runs as a single inline row. The menubar is about 40px tall (estimated), full-width and filled, with the logo and menus left and the CTA plus icons right. Desktop icon columns flank the window. At 375px, drop the icon columns, run the window edge-to-edge, set display to 30px and use a 48px section gap. Density: compact.

## Desktop Metaphor Discipline

The thesis is that the website is a desktop. A window sits over wallpaper, flanked by shortcut icons and topped by a menubar, and every component inherits that logic. Windows get shadows, keys get ledges, and metadata is set in the system mono. Three moves would break it: scrolling sections that span full-bleed edge-to-edge, a sticky translucent header that replaces the menubar, or marketing illustrations that do not look like running software. To extend the system, add new pages as new windows, sized 672px for documents and 1200px for apps. New features become new desktop icons with 16px white labels, and comparisons render as mockups of real UI. When in doubt, ask what an operating system would do. A modal is a window, a notification is a 4px-radius toast, and a settings panel uses tabs, not cards.

## Keycap Depth Grammar

Depth is semantic here, not ornamental. Hard zero-blur offsets are reserved for things you press. The amber key lifts its #eb9d2a face 2px over a #cd8407 ledge, and the white key rests on a 2.5px rgba(210, 211, 204, 1) step. Soft blur shadows belong only to things that float, such as the window, setup panel and menus. Mixing the two breaks the grammar: a blur on a button makes it feel like a panel, and a hard ledge on a card makes it look clickable. Extend the grammar by giving toggles and segmented controls the same 2px ledge and the same #b17816 border. Keep collapse-on-press at exactly translateY(0), so every pressable object shares one physical travel distance.

## Olive-Gray Neutrality

Every neutral leans slightly green-yellow: #eeefe9, #e5e7e0, #bfc1b7, #9ea096, #65675e and #23251d. That cast ties the chrome to the painted wallpaper and makes amber feel native rather than applied. The most common mistake is importing a stock Tailwind gray ramp, which the extracted #111827 and #374151 inheritances already hint at. Cool slate grays would make the window look pasted onto the backdrop. Extend the ramp by holding the hue near 75° and adjusting only lightness. A new mid step between #9ea096 and #bfc1b7 lands around #afb1a6. Tints of the accent should be made by alpha at 10% or 40%, as the badges do, rather than by inventing new solid hexes.

## Similar Brands

- **Raycast** — Both render product marketing as native desktop software, with window chrome, keyboard-key buttons and system-mono metadata. Raycast stays dark and glassy where PostHog runs warm and paper-light.
- **Basecamp** — Both share an opinionated, hand-annotated tone with yellow highlighter emphasis on headline phrases. Basecamp uses a serif-adjacent editorial layout instead of an operating-system frame.
- **Gumroad** — Both build tactile buttons from hard zero-blur offsets and bordered faces. Gumroad pushes it to full neo-brutalism with black 2px borders, while PostHog's 1px bronze edge is restrained.
- **Mixpanel** — A direct product-analytics competitor that shows dense event tables and charts as hero proof. Mixpanel's corporate violet and pill buttons are the convention PostHog's olive neutrals and keycaps reject.
- **Notion** — Both rest on a warm off-white canvas, with hairline-separated blocks and near-black #111111-range text. Notion stays monochrome and flat with no window metaphor.
